question: Q3 2026 revenue growth fell to 0.75% and profit fell 8%. Does the 113.55 yuan price (S1 quote, 20261120) price the end of growth, or a pause?
why_this_question: First round on this company in this session. Revenue growth is falling quickly while the price has dropped, and the 2026 share issue makes the old comparison muddy.

statements.text: Revenue growth went 21%, 11%, then under 1% in Q3, and Q3 profit fell 8%. The market cap is down 40% since last December, but that is muddy: the share count went from 5.2 to 7.3 亿 and about 99 亿 of cash came in. So my question is simple: does 113.55 yuan price the end of growth, or just a pause?

evidence.claim: Revenue growth 21.5%, 11.3%, 0.75% in Q1–Q3 2026; Q3 profit −7.8%
Share count 5.20 → 7.34 亿; 98.85 亿 capital contribution in Q1

statements.text: Before the price, I'd like to know if this is a blip. Compare each quarter with two years ago, not one: it was up 69% in Q1, 49% in Q2, 31% in Q3. That is a steady slowing, not one bad quarter. If I were the bear, I'd say the 2025 summer filled the shelves and 2026 is the hangover.

challenges.point: One slow quarter is not evidence of a pause; the slowing has run three quarters.

statements.text: Then let me ask what slowed. If they had cut price to hold volume, gross margin would show it. It did the opposite: 45.7% in Q3 against 45.2% a year ago. So the same price sells fewer bottles. That is a demand or shelf problem, not a price war, and I trust it more than a margin story. I'd still watch how often the company needs promotions to get the bottle out.

evidence.claim: Gross margin Q3 2026 45.7% vs 45.2% in Q3 2025

statements.text: What I notice on the cash side is that dealers have not blinked. Customer prepayments were 50.9 亿 at September, about 43% above a year ago, and nearly unchanged from June. Operating cash for nine months is up 13%. If dealers feared too much stock, they would prepay less. I read that as a pause.

evidence.claim: Contract liabilities 50.90 vs 35.63 a year earlier; 51.30 in June

challenges.point: A hangover would show up in dealer prepayments first; they are not falling.

statements.text: I don't accept that. A prepayment is a dealer's promise to the company, not a sale to a drinker. Dealers who loaded up last summer still have to keep their contract. Prepayments tell us what dealers will order, which lags what customers buy. So I take your number as a lead, and the test is year-end: last year it was 59.7 亿. If that falls, I'm right.

concessions.point: Prepayments holding up is not what a channel in distress looks like.

statements.text: Now profit. Q3 profit before tax fell about 1 亿 from a year ago. Selling the drinks and running the business got better by about 1.7 亿: gross profit up 0.5, marketing down 1.1, admin up 0.45, net interest better by 0.55. What dragged it down, by about 2.6 亿, was investment and fair-value gains falling 1.5 and a 1.1 亿 other financial cost. So the stall hit sales, not the profit engine.

evidence.claim: Q3 pretax profit 16.77 vs 17.76; fair-value + investment income −1.46; other financial cost −1.13 (derived)

statements.text: Careful with 'marketing down 1.1'. Marketing was 17% of sales in Q1 and Q2 and only 13% in Q3, and gross margin jumped to 49.7% in Q2. Those two move in opposite directions. Take them together and the margin is 32% in both Q2 and Q3, against 30% last year. Over nine months, marketing is actually higher than last year, 16.0% against 15.5%. So the company did not cut marketing; it moved the cost around. The gain is about gross margin, 47.5% against 45.2%.

evidence.claim: Gross margin less selling ratio: Q2 32.5%, Q3 32.3% vs 30.9%, 29.9% in 2025

challenges.point: The 'cost cut' is mostly timing between two lines, so I would not call it discipline.

concessions.point: The Q3 gain in profit is not a sign of a healthier sales engine.

statements.text: Fair, I accept that: the improvement is margin, and it comes from the product mix and cost side, not from squeezing marketing. Now the price. I take profit after the last four quarters of 48 亿 and charge 8% on the 186 亿 of equity. The market cap of 834 亿 then needs about 2.75% growth forever in residual earnings. At year-end the same method needed 5.0%. At 6% it needs almost nothing, at 10% about 5%.

evidence.claim: Implied perpetual growth in residual earnings: 0.3% / 2.75% / 5.2% at r = 6% / 8% / 10%; 5.0% at 20251231 and 8%
evidence.source: derived: S1 quote 20261120, S2 raw statements; workpaper

evidence.claim: Residual earnings = earnings less a required-return charge on book value

concessions.point: Margin, not marketing, is the profit gain.

statements.text: I'd push back on charging 8% on the new cash. About 99 亿 sits there earning interest of roughly 3%, yet the formula treats it as a business that must earn 8%. Take it out of both sides and the implied growth drops to about 2%. That is a modest ask, though it depends on the cash being returned or used well. It is also dependent on what the company does with the money, which nobody here knows.

evidence.claim: Excluding the 98.85 亿 raised from price and equity (and its interest), implied growth at 8% ≈ 2%

challenges.point: Charging 8% on idle cash overstates the growth the market needs.

statements.text: One more fact fits the pause view and one doesn't. Capital spending fell to 2.9 亿 in Q3 from about 6 亿 in each of the first two quarters, so management is not building for a boom. Per my reading of the 2004 letter, a share is worth future cash, not earnings, so I care that cash is up while the building slows. Q4 capex tells us whether that is a decision or a timing.

evidence.claim: Capex Q3 2.94 vs 6.95 a year ago; 6.00 and 5.35 in Q1, Q2
Shares are worth the present value of future cash flows, not earnings
evidence.source: SRC Amazon Shareholder Letter 2004.html, opening paragraphs

statements.text: Here is my bear case in one line: three quarters of slowing, the biggest cost swing was moved between lines, and 3.5 亿 of financial cost nobody can explain. What would change my mind is Q4 revenue above last year's weak 40.3 亿 and dealer prepayments holding near 60 亿 at year-end. Until then I don't know it is a pause. I do accept that the price doesn't ask for zero growth.

evidence.claim: Other (non-interest) financial cost 3.55 in nine months of 2026 vs about zero in 2025
evidence.source: derived: fin_exp − (interest expense − interest income), S2 raw_income

concessions.point: At 8% or less, the price does not assume growth ends.

disagreements.topic: Do dealer prepayments (+43% yoy, flat since June) show a pause?

positions.jeff-bezos: Yes, dealers are not cutting orders.
positions.li-lu: No, prepayments lag sell-through; the year-end figure is the test.

disagreements.topic: Should the 99 亿 raised be charged an 8% return?

positions.stephen-penman: Yes, it is part of equity; 2.75% implied growth.
positions.warren-buffett: No, it is idle cash; about 2%.

disagreements.resolution: Both numbers are shown; the use of the money decides it.

disagreements.topic: Was Q3 profit helped by a marketing cut?

positions.warren-buffett: Marketing and gross margin offset; nine-month ratio is up.

disagreements.resolution: Timing between two lines; profit gain is margin.

conclusion.answer: The price does not assume growth ends: at 8% it needs about 2.75% perpetual growth in residual earnings (about 2% if the new cash and its interest are excluded), against 5.0% at year-end. Whether Q3 is a pause or the start of a lasting slowdown cannot be settled from one quarter; the panel leans to a pause on dealer prepayments and margins and stays unsure because growth has slowed three quarters in a row. The profit gain is gross margin, not a marketing cut.
what_would_change_our_mind: Q4 2026 revenue below the 40.31 亿 base
Year-end dealer prepayments well below the 59.74 亿 of last year
A 2026 announcement showing the 99 亿 is not held for use in the business
open_questions: What is the 3.55 亿 of non-interest financial cost in nine months of 2026?
What will the 99 亿 be used for?
Bonus issue or placement behind the move to 7.34 亿 shares, which is not in local data

next_question_candidates: Does Q4 2026 revenue clear the 40.31 亿 base and do prepayments hold?
What is the other financial cost and what will the 99 亿 earn?
